questions.enonce_markdown:
What are:

(i) Endocrine glands

(ii) Exocrine glands? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Endocrine glands** are **ductless glands** that **secrete hormones directly into the blood stream**, which carries them to the target organs. Examples: pituitary, thyroid, adrenal glands, islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, ovaries and testes.

(ii) **Exocrine glands** are glands that have **ducts** and **secrete their products (enzymes, sweat, saliva, mucus, etc.) through the ducts** onto a surface or into a cavity, not into the blood. Examples: salivary glands, sweat glands, gastric glands, the liver (bile), the pancreas (pancreatic juice).

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw an outline of the human body, showing the positions of the major endocrine glands. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Diagram to be drawn by the candidate: the outline of the head, neck and trunk of the human body, with the glands marked in the right places, each with a label line, and a title.*

**What to draw and label (from top to bottom):**

- **Pituitary gland**: at the base of the brain, under the hypothalamus.
- **Thyroid gland**: in the neck, in front of the trachea (windpipe), just below the larynx; the small **parathyroid glands** are on its back.
- **Thymus gland**: in the upper chest, behind the sternum, above the heart.
- **Adrenal glands**: one on top of each kidney.
- **Pancreas (islets of Langerhans)**: in the abdomen, below the stomach, in the loop of the duodenum.
- **Ovaries** (in a woman): in the lower abdomen on each side of the uterus; **testes** (in a man): in the scrotum, outside the abdomen.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe how the human kidney regulates the water contents of body fluids. *(11 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The regulation of the water content of the blood and body fluids is called **osmoregulation**. It is controlled by the **hypothalamus**, the **pituitary gland** and the **hormone ADH (antidiuretic hormone)**, by **negative feedback**.

**Background:** blood is filtered in the **glomerulus (ultrafiltration)**; in the **proximal convoluted tubule** all the glucose, amino acids and much of the water and salts are **reabsorbed**; the **loop of Henle** builds up a high salt concentration in the medulla; the **distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct** are where the final amount of water reabsorbed is adjusted.

**1. When the body has too little water** (dehydration, hot weather, sweating, little drinking):

- The **blood becomes more concentrated** (its water potential falls).
- **Osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus** detect this, and the **posterior pituitary gland releases more ADH** into the blood.
- ADH makes the walls of the **distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct more permeable to water**.
- **More water is reabsorbed** into the blood by osmosis, so the kidney produces a **small volume of concentrated (dark) urine**.
- The blood water content returns to normal.

**2. When the body has too much water** (after drinking a lot of water):

- The **blood becomes dilute** (its water potential rises); the hypothalamus detects this, and **less ADH is released**.
- The walls of the distal tubule and collecting duct become **less permeable to water**.
- **Less water is reabsorbed**, so a **large volume of dilute (pale) urine** is produced.
- The blood water content returns to normal.

In this way the **water content of the blood is kept constant (homeostasis)**.
